goal.en: Specify the selected business behavior precisely enough to implement and independently accept it.

purpose.en: Read current target, ancestor scope, refs, dependencies, assertions and validator freshness. For an explicitly new target, absence is expected: inspect the nearest existing ancestor/workspace, then create only that selected scope. Preserve unaffected accepted content.

When source exists/is selected, resolve repository resource, actual checkout/root/HEAD and dirty state; read applicable instructions, manifests, owning code, callers and relevant tests. Greenfield/spec-only work records source not-yet-created and grounds intent in the user request; no invented repository or fact citation. Source implementation still needs an actual selected writable repository.

reads.path: current accepted user intent + supplied domain documents

purpose.en: Classify each statement as intent, observed fact, example, proposal, unknown or contradiction, with source citation/revision. Existing behavior does not authorize a new rule.
Read the JSON field contract and this operator procedure before authoring the .work payload.

Only when explicitly selected in a job matrix, read the exact cell ID, operation, immutable input bindings, requested output JSON shapes and required criteria. Standalone execution needs no fabricated matrix request. A template is not authority for extra effects.

reads.path: profiles/registry.json + selected runtime execution profile + actual host tools/model

purpose.en: Select the actual host runtime codex or claude and this operator role from the V2-derived active profiles. Use current host model configuration; historical model names are not availability proof. Capabilities are the intersection of actual tools, selected profile policy, op permissions and existing task authority. Do not revive V2 dispatch chains, retired profiles or extra-agent permissions.

fields: body: Objective / Glossary / Actors & permissions / FR / NFR / Business rules / Non-business constraints / State transitions / Acceptance / Decisions / Open questions

content.en: FR rows: ID, actor, trigger, preconditions, input/schema, normal action/output, failure/denial, postcondition, priority, source and AC refs. NFR rows: metric, numeric target when decided, unit, workload, percentile/window, environment, measurement method and source; undecided targets stay unknown. BR rows: condition, decision, authority, affected transitions and exceptions. Technical/contractual constraints are separate from domain policy. Graph edits apply only to the explicitly selected approved scope: declare real prerequisite node IDs in dependsOn and semantic input node/resource IDs in refs. No catalogue-wide chain or new unrelated scope; finish all graph/spec changes before review proof. Store full structured requirements, ordered flows, codeImpacts, serviceImpacts, security, acceptance, sources, decisions and handoff in extensions.work3.specification. Keep reserved core metadata unchanged; .work is the canonical root.
Record requirement-to-acceptance coverage, concrete source observations and unresolved contradictions; a specification review is not implementation evidence.

Only for a selected job matrix, return the exact request-bound result. Populate every declared cell output with actual canonical Work/source/runtime references or produced JSON artifacts from this job; retain real artifact bytes and hashes. Do not rename/regenerate upstream expectations. Missing required output/evidence remains blocked or failed and cannot advance. The selected request freezes output field schemas before execution.

action.en: Resolve the canonical .work workspace and selected business leaf. Research accepted intent, domain documents and current FE/BE callers at exact revisions. Classify every citation as accepted intent, observed source, proposal or unknown; source behavior never approves policy. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Write objective, glossary, actors, ownership, FR/BR and measurable NFRs. Separate output from persisted effects and technical constraints from business policy. Preserve unknown numeric targets with the decision owner; never invent targets.

Write ordered flows with entry, actor, prerequisites, request, response/error, transitions, guards, side effects and postconditions. Cover success, invalid/denied input, retry, duplicate, concurrency, cancellation and recovery where relevant; mark non-applicability with reasons.

Trace each flow to observed UI/API/module/store callers and affected services. Record a preliminary codeImpacts/serviceImpacts inventory, source citations, direct versus transitive impact, preserve/change/review disposition and unknowns. This is architecture input, not authorization to edit every discovered file.

Specify actor-action-resource permissions, tenant/owner boundaries, sensitive-data handling and abuse cases. Give each security requirement an observable denial/no-side-effect acceptance scenario; do not mistake a disabled UI control for server enforcement.

Assign stable requirement/flow/AC IDs and Given/When/Then expectations, proof owner and instrument. Record decisions to implement/preserve/defer/not-applicable with authority and revisit condition. Store the full JSON payload in extensions.work3.specification and real dependencies/refs in core fields, not hidden prose. Author canonical user journeys and journeyCoverage links to flow/AC IDs using the shared journey contract; preserve accepted journeys unchanged in architecture. Do not convert internal service hops into UI actions. Browser-free scope may use an empty array only when no UAT acceptance is assigned.

Validate coverage and .work bindings; review all unresolved decisions together. Output requirements, ordered flows, acceptance, preliminary impact and security inputs for architecture/draw/planning. No automatic secondary call is defined for this op; report a missing decision and do not invent a helper. Complete only this reviewed business scope. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts.

requirement.en: Run workspace validation; every cited ID/path exists or is explicitly proposed, required assertions are covered, input bindings are current, and an honest not-run/fail cannot earn done.
Each applicable FR/NFR/BR has acceptance IDs and source intent; no vague fast/secure/user-friendly NFR is accepted as measurable. Implementation/UAT status is untouched.
Every selected flow resolves cited code/service impact, security controls and acceptance; proposed/unknown facts remain explicit. Validate the JSON specification and .work before review completion.

condition.en: A required rule, actor permission, numeric target or acceptance result has no authoritative decision.
Accepted sources conflict; preserve both citations and ask the actual owner, never average them.

A declared prerequisite is not effectively done, or a required declared input/scope is missing. Report node/resource IDs and propose a separately selected graph update when needed; never run predecessors or weaken dependsOn/refs/required to proceed.
